correctness.rationale: At each midpoint the Sidon property leaves exactly one unordered pair. Its off-diagonal contribution is an elementary p-point sampled cosine sum; the odd-grid trigonometric identity yields the exact norm. Algebraic expansion gives a termwise nonnegative deficit and forces all equality cases. A quadratic-graph Sidon proof holds over every odd finite field, and Wigner Plancherel supplies the sqrt(N) reference bound. The embedded script directly checks four supports and multiple phase/magnitude choices; finite samples are not presented as the proof.

value.rationale: The Wigner L1 mass (and its logarithm, mana) is a natural measurable quasiprobability-negativity invariant. The finding determines that invariant exactly throughout a large structured class with arbitrary coefficient amplitudes and phases, including complete sharp equality and an explicit stability deficit. The quadratic Sidon construction gives nontrivial pure states in every odd-prime square Hilbert dimension with mass growing proportionally to the optimal universal sqrt(N) scale, not merely an arbitrary small finite table. It does not claim a downstream resource theorem beyond these precise invariants.
